target_customer: Office tenants searching for commercial space, with landlords and brokers as listing sources
problem: Searching for office space was slow and opaque because listings were scattered and poorly presented.
business_model: Free search site for tenants, monetized through landlord and broker listings and leads

founders.name: Jason Freedman
founders.background_notes: Also founded GP Orange Collective per YC page.

competitors.name: LoopNet
competitors.what: Largest commercial real estate listings site

competitors.name: CoStar
competitors.what: Commercial real estate data and listings

competitors.name: Cityfeet
competitors.what: Commercial real estate MLS owned by LoopNet

technical_complexity.rationale: A listings search site, with the hard part being data collection and photography rather than software.

defensibility.rationale: Photography and listing data built over time helped, but incumbents held the listing supply and a rival could copy the interface.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept their position, and 42Floors was sold to Knotel in July 2018 for an undisclosed amount.

market_need_then: Commercial listings were dominated by dated sites and TechCrunch in March 2012 called office search painful, with demand for free, well photographed listings.

branding.domain_note: Used 42floors.com, which now redirects to commercialcafe.com.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in startup press but no evidence of consumer brand pull or community around the name.

pivots.to: National search engine for office space
pivots.why: Coverage said it discontinued broker services to focus on search, date approximate.

outcome_analysis: 42Floors launched in March 2012 as a free office search site against LoopNet and CoStar, raised 5 million dollars in late 2012 and 12.3 million dollars led by NEA in January 2013, then expanded nationally. It reached about 60 people but did not become a category leader and was bought by Knotel in July 2018 for an undisclosed price, partly for its data and a blockchain listing plan.
notes: Series A date varies by source between September and November 2012. Total funding figures conflict across trackers (17.7 million to 22.3 million dollars). Search results also mentioned a Yardi acquisition in December 2021, unverified and not recorded. YC page batch label shows Winter 2012 while a YC blog post says S12. Founder education not found. Success factor code other because no listed driver is sourced.
